channel.title: CNS Feed
channel.description: Aggregated research articles from Cell, Nature, and Science.

item.title: Cell: Efficient amyloid-β degradation in Alzheimer’s disease using SPYTACs
item.description: SPYTAC is a synthetic peptide-programmed targeted protein degradation platform harnessing LRP1 to drive lysosomal degradation of extracellular amyloid-β in the brain and periphery. In 5×FAD mice, SPYTAC treatment efficiently degrades amyloid-β, preserves neurons, and improves cognition with reduced neuroinflammation and microhemorrhage when compared with antibody therapy.

item.title: Cell: Genetically encoded fluorescent reporters to visualize α-synuclein pathology in live brain
item.description: The development of genetically encoded fluorescent reporters, along with their corresponding knock-in mouse lines for labeling α-Syn inclusions, enables diverse applications in studying the propagation and pathological effects of α-Syn inclusions in the live brain.

item.title: Cell: Restoring circadian rhythms in the hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus reverses aging biomarkers and extends lifespan in male mice
item.description: Enhancing circadian amplitude in mouse hypothalamic paraventricular nucleus neurons by 3′-deoxyadenosine treatment alleviates age-related pathologies and extends lifespan.

item.title: Nature: Shared neural substrates of prosocial and parenting behaviours
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10327-8 Shared neural substrates of prosocial and parenting behaviours

item.title: Nature: Heart surgery with quick-setting magnetic fluid could prevent strokes
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00742-2 Injectable fluid safely fills area in which blood clots can form, in animal trials — plus, strong evidence that an elusive form of diamond has been made in the lab.

item.title: Nature: Magnetic gel injected into the heart could stop strokes
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00740-4 The hydrogel-based plug blocks a part of the heart to cut stroke risk and was shown to be effective in rats and a pig.

item.title: Nature: Genome modelling and design across all domains of life with Evo 2
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10176-5 Evo 2 is an artificial intelligence-based biological foundation model trained on 9 trillion DNA base pairs spanning all domains of life that predicts functional properties from genomic sequences and provides a rich generative model for researchers in biology.

item.title: Nature: DICER cleavage fidelity is governed by 5′-end binding pockets
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10211-5 Cryo-electron microscopy and massively parallel assays shed light on the mechanism by which DICER, a key enzyme in the RNase III family, cleaves RNA at precise locations to produce small RNAs.

item.title: Nature: Limited thermal tolerance in tropical insects and its genomic signature
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10155-w A survey of tropical insect populations and thermal tolerance limits indicates that species from lowland areas have low capacity to survive increased temperatures, and that thermal tolerance is limited by fundamental properties of protein architecture.

item.title: Nature: A metabolic alarmin from keratinocytes potentiates systemic humoral immunity
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10167-6 Farnesyl pyrophosphate—a mevalonate pathway metabolic intermediate—is an endogenous alarmin that enhances IgG antibody responses through keratinocyte-derived IL-6 and CCL20.

item.title: Nature: Long-term thrombus-free left atrial appendage occlusion via magnetofluids
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-025-10091-1 In the presence of a sufficient magnetic field, magnetofluids can resist high-speed blood flow, offering a personalized and complete strategy for left atrial appendage occlusion.

item.title: Nature: Lipid metabolism drives dietary effects on T cell ferroptosis and immunity
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10193-4 The susceptibility of mouse and human T cells to ferroptosis is determined by the balance of systemic polyunsaturated and monounsaturated fatty acids, highlighting a key role for lipid metabolism and dietary composition in regulating T cell function.

item.title: Nature: Merlin: a computed tomography vision–language foundation model and dataset
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10181-8 Merlin, a vision–language foundation model trained on a large dataset of paired CT scans, patient record data and radiology reports, demonstrates strong performance across model architectures, diagnostic and prognostic tasks, and external sites.

item.title: Nature: Microbiota-mediated induction of beige adipocytes in response to dietary cues
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10205-3 In mice, a low-protein diet leads to a gut-microbiota-driven remodelling of adipose tissue towards brown fat, showing that gut microorganisms have a role in detecting and responding to a lack of protein.

item.title: Nature: Mechanism of co-transcriptional cap snatching by influenza polymerase
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10189-0 Structural and biochemical studies of influenza virus RNA-dependent RNA polymerase (FluPol) in complex with transcribing host RNA polymerase II reveal the molecular mechanisms of RNA cap snatching by FluPol.

item.title: Nature: Cell-free chromatin state tracing reveals disease origin and therapy responses
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10224-0 cf-EpiTracing enables automated profiling of histone modifications in cell-free DNA from human plasma, allowing identification of the cells of origin and disease diagnosis.

item.title: Nature: The oldest articulated bony fish from the early Silurian period
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10125-2 A tiny, articulated, near-complete osteichthyan from the early Silurian Chongqing Lagerstätte, represents the oldest osteichthyan occurrence including microfossils, and the earliest articulated remains of any bony fish in the fossil record.

item.title: Nature: Bulk hexagonal diamond
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10212-4 The synthesis of millimetre-sized phase-pure hexagonal diamond, a polymorph of cubic diamond, by compressing highly oriented pyrolytic graphite under high pressures and temperatures is reported, providing new insight into the graphite-to-diamond transformation pathway.

item.title: Nature: Sea level much higher than assumed in most coastal hazard assessments
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10196-1 Meta-analyses on a global scale show that the measured coastal mean sea level is higher than assumed in most coastal hazard assessments.

item.title: Nature: A glucocorticoid–FAS axis controls immune evasion during metastatic seeding
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10222-2 Glucocorticoid receptor activation is a key driver of resistance of triple-negative breast cancer to both CD8+ T cells and natural killer cells during initial metastatic seeding.

item.title: Nature: The molecular basis of force selectivity by PIEZO2
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10182-7 PIEZO2 is intrinsically more rigid than PIEZO1, and disparate mechanical stimuli paradoxically evoke opposite conformational and gating responses in each channel.

item.title: Nature: Advancing operational global aerosol forecasting with machine learning
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10234-y Reliable 5-day, 3-hourly forecasts of aerosol optical components and surface concentrations are obtained in 1 minute using a machine-learning-driven forecasting system.

item.title: Nature: Wind shear enhances soil moisture influence on rapid thunderstorm growth
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-025-10045-7 Analysis of millions of events over sub-Saharan Africa shows that wind shear amplifies the impact of soil moisture in triggering rapidly developing thunderstorms.

item.title: Nature: Structural basis of RNA-guided transcription by a dCas12f–σ E –RNAP complex
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10178-3 Cryogenic electron microscopy reveals how dCas12f with σE recruits RNAP to targeted DNA, initiating transcription at a fixed downstream distance, bypassing canonical −35 recognition and stabilizing the −10 element in an unusual manner.

item.title: Nature: Homologous recombination deficiency and hemizygosity drive resistance in breast cancer
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10197-0 Germline and somatic interactions define actionable genomic patterns driving acquired therapy resistance in breast cancer.

item.title: Nature: Exapted CRISPR–Cas12f homologues drive RNA-guided transcription
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10166-7 Specialized σ factors interact with nuclease-dead, CRISPR–Cas12f proteins to form potent, RNA-guided gene activation systems that function independently of fixed promoter motifs.

item.title: Nature: Wide-swath altimetry maps bank shapes and storage changes in global rivers
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10218-y Observations of river channel geometry and monthly water storage changes for 126,674 river reaches worldwide are derived from the first water year of the Surface Water and Ocean Topography satellite mission.

item.title: Nature: Largest Silurian fish illuminates the origin of osteichthyan characters
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-025-10008-y New findings from articulated head and trunk material of Megamastax amblyodus yield previously unseen morphological details of a Silurian stem osteichthyan.

item.title: Nature: Precancerous niche remodelling dictates nascent tumour persistence
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10157-8 A study investigating the emergence of squamous tumours in the upper gastrointestinal tract of the mouse shows that an initial tumour stress response triggers fibroblasts to remodel the underlying stroma, creating a fibronectin-rich precancerous niche that supports tumour survival.

item.title: Nature: Rising temperatures pose a threat to tropical insects
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00377-3 An assessment of sensitivity to increasing temperature for thousands of insect species in mountainous terrain reveals a risk of insect biodiversity loss in tropical lowlands.

item.title: Nature: Fresh claim of making elusive ‘hexagonal’ diamond is the strongest yet
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00711-9 After decades of debate, researchers say that they have found the clearest evidence yet for this rare form of carbon.

item.title: Nature: Stress-hormone signalling protects spreading cancer cells from immune system
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00650-5 Metastasis occurs when cancer cells spread to other organs and escape elimination by the immune system. Analysis reveals that these cells resist killing by immune cells by harnessing stress-hormone signalling through the glucocorticoid receptor, suggesting a potential therapeutic target for preventing metastasis.

item.title: Nature: AI can write genomes — how long until it creates synthetic life?
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00681-y The Evo2 genomic language model can generate short genome sequences, but scientists say further advances are needed to write genomes that will work inside living cells.

item.title: Nature: Magnetic fluid offers better seal in heart-plugging medical procedure
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00375-5 An injectable fluid has been used to close off part of the heart in animals — a potentially improved take on a procedure that prevents stroke in people with irregular heartbeats.

item.title: Nature: Funding from individual donors: lessons from the Epstein case
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00658-x Universities need to establish and empower compliance teams to ensure adherence to ethical funding policies.

item.title: Nature: A genetic switch turns off parental behaviour and drives infanticide in male striped mice
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00656-z Male parenting in mammals is highly variable, ranging from caring to neglectful and abusive. The brain and behaviour of the African striped mouse reveal that, in males, the social environment and expression level of the Agouti gene affect whether the animals will be hostile or caring towards pups.

item.title: Nature: Do wet or dry soils trigger thunderstorms? It depends on how the wind blows
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00376-4 Satellite data show that wind conditions affect the connection between soil moisture and thunderstorms, which could be used to inform forecasting.

item.title: Nature: Climate change and geopolitics threaten water supplies — but disaster is not inevitable
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00659-w The Indus Waters Treaty withstood several armed conflicts and a huge loss of glaciers. It should serve as a blueprint for others.

item.title: Nature: Cancer blood tests are everywhere. Do they really work?
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00661-2 Their makers claim they can detect dozens of cancer types — but some scientists say they could be missing many cancers or delivering the wrong diagnosis.

item.title: Nature: Skin cells boost distant antibody responses
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00379-1 How the skin enables immune defences is not fully clear. Now a pathway has been found in skin cells that boosts the production of antibodies to protect the whole body.

item.title: Nature: How a mathematician is cracking open Mexico’s powerful drug cartels
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00299-0 Rafael Prieto-Curiel explains how his models of organized crime could improve public safety in his home country.

item.title: Nature: Under pressure: the reality of Mexico’s research system
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00442-x Researcher Oscar Xavier Guerrero Gutiérrez speaks out about the unstable conditions that Mexican scientists face — and what can be done to help.

item.title: Nature: Radiology AI makes consistent diagnoses using 3D images from different health centres
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00645-2 To meet the growing demand for radiology artificial-intelligence tools, a 3D vision–language model called Merlin was trained on abdominal computed-tomography scans, radiology reports and electronic health records. Merlin demonstrated stronger off-the-shelf performance than did other vision–language models across three hospital sites distinct from the initial training centre, highlighting its potential for broader clinical adoption.

item.title: Nature: Hunt for reactive metabolites uncovers unusual chemistry in a human pathogen
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00652-3 A workflow was developed to selectively capture bacterially produced compounds containing a reactive diazo chemical group. This enabled the discovery of two diazo-containing molecules from a bacterium that causes lung disease. Investigation of the bacterial synthesis of these molecules revealed an enzyme that constructs the diazo group, with broad synthetic applications.

item.title: Nature: All the world is staged
item.description: Nature, Published online: 04 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00131-9 Exits and entrances.

item.title: Nature: Genetically encoded assembly recorder temporally resolves cellular history
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10323-y Genetically encoded assembly recorder temporally resolves cellular history

item.title: Nature: Jam-packed star system is most compact of its kind ever found
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00667-w All four Sun-like stars would fit inside the area of Jupiter’s orbit.

item.title: Nature: Releasing open-weight AI in steps would alleviate risks
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00679-6 Releasing open-weight AI in steps would alleviate risks

item.title: Nature: From the first telephone to videoconferencing in 100 years
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00641-6 Scientists of the 1970s look to the past and future of telecommunications, and a rainbow against a blue sky dazzles a reader, in this week’s peek at Nature’s archive.

item.title: Nature: South Korea’s AI framework act focuses on rights and safety
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00678-7 South Korea’s AI framework act focuses on rights and safety

item.title: Nature: Climate research is global — risks and responsibilities should also be distributed
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00680-z Climate research is global — risks and responsibilities should also be distributed

item.title: Nature: Why ‘quantum proteins’ could be the next big thing in biology
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00662-1 Fluorescent proteins with a quantum upgrade could offer unprecedented views inside cells.

item.title: Nature: US climate actions must continue, despite setbacks
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00660-3 The United States has slammed the brakes on legal routes to limit greenhouse gases. But cities, states and businesses can keep pushing for a cleaner environment.

item.title: Nature: My relationship with my PhD supervisor has become toxic — what do I do?
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-025-04126-w A graduate student in China has become seriously depressed after facing frequent verbal abuse.

item.title: Nature: How infighting led the Maya civilization to catastrophic collapse
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00663-0 Fresh archaeological evidence hints at what caused the disappearance of this thriving ancient Mesoamerican culture.

item.title: Nature: See raining iguanas and coral from the inside out — February’s best science images
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00597-7 The month’s sharpest science shots, selected by Nature’s photo team.

item.title: Nature: Climate shocks, not just warming, threaten malaria control efforts in Africa
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00491-2 Climate change is expected to affect mosquito and parasite survival, reshaping malaria risk. But extreme weather could be a more immediate danger to disease control.

item.title: Nature: Hey ChatGPT, write me a fictional paper: these LLMs are willing to commit academic fraud
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00595-9 Mainstream chatbots presented varying levels of resistance to deliberate requests for fabrication, study finds.

item.title: Nature: How can fast-evolving DNA retain a fundamental function in cell division?
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00629-2 In a dividing cell, chromosome pairs are pulled apart thanks to attachment sites called centromeres. Yeast genomes reveal key steps in how centromeres have evolved.

item.title: Nature: Going ‘beyond GDP’ should not mean sidelining the SDGs
item.description: Nature, Published online: 03 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00657-y The UN Sustainable Development Goals represent a carefully-crafted road map for future human and planetary prosperity.

item.title: Nature: BCDX2–CX3 and DX2–CX3 complexes assemble and stabilize RAD51 filaments
item.description: Nature, Published online: 02 March 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10314-z BCDX2–CX3 and DX2–CX3 complexes assemble and stabilize RAD51 filaments

item.title: Nature: The squeal of peeling tape, explained
item.description: Nature, Published online: 02 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00516-w Weak shock waves triggered by micro-cracks in the adhesive layer of tape cause it to screech when being unspooled from its roll.

item.title: Nature: Audio long read: Many people have no mental imagery. What’s going on in their brains?
item.description: Nature, Published online: 02 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00626-5 People with aphantasia are offering brain scientists a window into consciousness.

item.title: Nature: The hidden lives behind China’s great Internet firewall
item.description: Nature, Published online: 02 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00664-z The country’s tightly controlled digital ecosystem is replete with human stories and acts of subtle resistance.

item.title: Nature: AI agents are ‘aeroplanes for the mind’: five ways to ensure that scientists are responsible pilots
item.description: Nature, Published online: 02 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00665-y As artificial-intelligence systems take on more of the scientific workflow, the central goal should not be complete automation, but designing platforms that preserve creativity, responsibility and surprise.

item.title: Nature: Earth’s oldest crystals suggest an early start for plate tectonics
item.description: Nature, Published online: 02 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00628-3 The planet’s crust could already have been churning 3.3 billion years ago.

item.title: Nature: ‘No one quite like her’: meet the female colleagues who inspire these award-winning women in science
item.description: Nature, Published online: 02 March 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00666-x To mark International Women’s Day, Nature asked winners of its awards programmes to nominate a colleague who brings out the best in them.

item.title: Cell: Pyruvate is a natural suppressor of interferon signaling by inducing STAT1 protein pyruvylation
item.description: Yibo et al. identify protein pyruvylation as a post-translational modification that can modulate immune signaling and host antiviral response.

item.title: Cell: High-resolution in situ structures of hantavirus glycoprotein tetramers
item.description: The cryo-EM structures of Andes hantavirus (ANDV) glycoprotein tetramers, dimers of tetramers, and ADI-65534 Fab complexes on eVLPs unveil the molecular basis of New World hantavirus glycoprotein architecture, acid-induced membrane fusion, and antibody-mediated neutralization. Immunization with repRNA encoding ANDV-VLPs elicits high neutralizing-antibody titers.

item.title: Cell: Citrate clearance is a major function of aconitase 2 in the canonical TCA cycle
item.description: Beyond its traditional role in supporting bioenergetic and biosynthetic demands, the canonical TCA cycle is also essential for nutrient clearance. When pyruvate oxidation and citrate production increase, aconitase 2 becomes essential to prevent mitochondrial citrate accumulation, which can trigger the integrated stress response and impair cell fitness.

item.title: Nature: Editorial Expression of Concern: The gene product Murr1 restricts HIV-1 replication in resting CD4+ lymphocytes
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 February 2026; doi:10.1038/s41586-026-10308-x Editorial Expression of Concern: The gene product Murr1 restricts HIV-1 replication in resting CD4+ lymphocytes

item.title: Nature: Briefing chat: Pokémon turns 30 — how Pikachu and pals inspired generations of researchers
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00674-x Nature staff discuss some of the week’s top science news.

item.title: Nature: Brain mysteries and Bronze Age diplomacy: Books in brief
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00621-w Andrew Robinson reviews five of the best science picks.

item.title: Nature: White House stalls release of approved US science budgets
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00601-0 The US Congress rejected sweeping cuts to science agencies. But the NIH, the NSF and NASA have had their spending slowed.

item.title: Nature: I will continue the fight for environmental justice in Black communities
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00538-4 Nicknamed the father of environmental justice, Robert Bullard argues that researchers in the field have more reason than ever to back up their work with action.

item.title: Nature: Pokémon turns 30 — how the fictional pocket monsters shaped science
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00441-y The Japanese media sensation has inspired generations of researchers in fields as diverse as evolution, biodiversity and research integrity.

item.title: Nature: Is a ‘selfish gene’ making a Utah family have twice as many boys as girls?
item.description: Nature, Published online: 27 February 2026; doi:10.1038/d41586-026-00505-z Genealogy study claims first conclusive case of sex ‘distortion’ in humans — but not all researchers are convinced.

Science: Organism-wide cellular dynamics and epigenomic remodeling in mammalian aging
Science: Imbalance in gut microbial interactions as a marker of health and disease
Science: A cellular basis for the mammalian nocturnal-diurnal switch
Science: Different DNA repair pathways support intact or truncated insertions by R2 retrotransposon protein
Science: Reconstitution of sex determination and the testicular niche using mouse pluripotent stem cells
Science: Cryo–electron microscopic visualization of RAD51 filament assembly and end-capping by XRCC3-RAD51C-RAD51D-XRCC2
Science: Hafnium oxide interface stabilization for efficient, photothermally stable perovskite solar cells
Science: Interbreeding between Neanderthals and modern humans was strongly sex biased
Science: OsWRI1a coordinates systemic growth responses to nitrogen availability in rice
Science: Organocatalyst-controlled stereoselective head-to-tail macrocyclizations
Science: Concurrent L1 retrotransposition events promote reciprocal translocations in human tumorigenesis
Cell: Large-scale proteomics across neurological disorders uncovers biomarker panel and targets in multiple sclerosis
item.description: Deep proteome profiling of over 5,000 cerebrospinal fluid samples by mass spectrometry maps protein alterations across major neurological disorders, resolving key sources of variation as well as shared and disease-specific signatures. This framework yields a 22-protein assay that improves the differential diagnosis of multiple sclerosis from other inflammatory conditions, particularly in diagnostically challenging oligoclonal band-negative individuals.

item.title: Cell: Vitamin B2 and B3 nutrigenomics reveals a therapy for NAXD disease
item.description: A nutrigenomics framework identifies genetic diseases amenable to vitamin B2 and B3 therapies. This approach nominates vitamin B3 as a therapy for NAXD deficiency, a lethal neurodevelopmental disorder. In this Naxd KO mouse model, vitamin B3 rescues NAD(P)(H) metabolism, prevents brain pathology, and extends lifespan by more than 40-fold.

item.title: Cell: Whole-organ and whole-body 3D atlases enable cellome-wide profiling
item.description: Whole-organ and whole-body atlases at single-cell resolution enable quantitative cellome-wide analysis across development, physiology, and pathology.

item.title: Cell: The MicrobeAtlas database: Global trends and insights into Earth’s microbial ecosystems
item.description: MicrobeAtlas ( www.microbeatlas.org ) is an integrated, reference-based resource for truly planet-wide microbiomics, analyzing hundreds of thousands of microbial lineages across diverse environments, conditions, and technologies.

item.title: Cell: Nuclear speckles enable processing of RNA from GC-rich isochores
item.description: Nuclear speckles are key subnuclear structures that regulate gene expression in GC-rich regions. This work shows that the evolution and expansion of core speckle proteins were crucial for the increased GC content seen in amniote genomes.

item.title: Cell: A regulatory network promotes apoplastic alkalinization to prime plant immunity in tissues distal to site of infection
item.description: Pathogen-exposed plant cells communicate with neighboring cells through apoplastic alkalinization and phytocytokines, which jointly propagate from the pathogen-exposed local tissue to distal tissues, providing a warning system for robust defenses and disease resistance.

item.title: Cell: Editing strigolactone hormone receptor for robust antiviral silencing in rice
item.description: Precise genome editing of the rice strigolactone receptor DWARF14 confers robust, transgene-free antiviral resistance by blocking viral suppression of endogenous RNA silencing, offering a promising strategy for durable disease protection without a yield penalty.

item.title: Cell: Fungal-derived cellobiose metabolic pathway fuels T cells to bypass intratumoral glucose competition
item.description: Equipping T cells with fungal enzymes to utilize cellobiose (a safe and natural disaccharide of glucose obtained from the wood polymer cellulose) enhances their viability and effector function in tumor microenvironments where glucose concentrations are constrained.

item.title: Cell: LUMI-lab: A foundation model-driven autonomous platform enabling discovery of ionizable lipid designs for mRNA delivery
item.description: LUMI lab is a foundation model-driven self-driving platform that autonomously discovers ionizable lipids for mRNA delivery. Iterative active learning uncovered brominated tails as a potent structural motif that enables efficient and safe pulmonary mRNA delivery.

item.title: Cell: A GPX1-OSBPL8 axis mediates noncanonical in vivo ferroptosis and cancer growth suppression
item.description: An in vivo , noncanonical ferroptosis pathway, critical for tumor supression, is driven by reactive oxygen species-induced phosphatidic acid peroxidation at the ER under the control of the GPX1-OSBPL8 signaling axis.

item.title: Science: Matching sounds to shapes: Evidence of the bouba-kiki effect in naïve baby chicks
Science: Ribosomal RNA expansion segments mediate the oligomerization of inactive animal ribosomes
Science: Evolution of error correction through a need for speed
Science: Carbonated ultramafic igneous rocks in Jezero crater, Mars
Science: Termination of the integrated stress response
Cell: Brain-wide mapping of oligodendrocyte organization, oligodendrogenesis, and myelin injury
item.description: Generation of brain-wide oligodendrocyte atlases across aging, disease, sex, and strain reveals striking regional differences in myelin abundance, resilience, and vulnerability. Integration with transcriptomic and ultrastructural data identifies factors that may shape this diverse oligodendrocyte patterning.

item.title: Cell: Genomic atlas of Bifidobacterium infantis and B. longum informs infant probiotic design
item.description: A global genomic survey of infant gut bifidobacteria shows that B. infantis remains highly prevalent and diverse in infants from low- and middle-income countries but scarce in Western, industrialized populations and poorly represented in current probiotics. This genomic and culture collection catalogs geo-specific B. infantis strains and provides a blueprint for developing probiotics tailored to local diets and populations to support infant health.

item.title: Cell: Unified modeling of 3D molecular generation via atomic interactions with PocketXMol
item.description: A versatile, atom-level generative AI model enables unified pocket-interacting tasks, from docking to de novo design, and demonstrates robust experimental validation for both small-molecule and peptide therapeutics.

item.title: Cell: Liver exerkine reverses aging- and Alzheimer’s-related memory loss via vasculature
item.description: Liver exercise factor GPLD1 rejuvenates blood-brain barrier integrity and reverses cognitive impairments in aging and Alzheimer’s disease models by targeting GPI-anchored proteins on brain endothelial cells.

item.title: Cell: A circadian rheostat drives proton electrochemical gradients to optimize cell-type-specific growth in Arabidopsis
item.description: The clock component CCA1 functions as a molecular rheostat, fine-tuning cell-type-specific electrochemical gradients to optimize carbon allocation and the timely coordination of shoot and root growth balance.

item.title: Cell: Tuning the sensitivity of mechanosensory receptors through histidine scanning
item.description: Histidine scanning represents a broadly applicable technique for the identification of critical interaction sites within TCRs and other mechanosensory receptors to enhance receptor signaling strength and augment therapeutic efficacy via the catch bond mechanism.

item.title: Cell: Giant DNA viruses encode a hallmark translation initiation complex of eukaryotic life
item.description: Giant DNA viruses encode a cap-binding complex homologous to eIF4F, the defining translation-initiation complex of eukaryotes. The viral cap-binding complex is required for viral protein synthesis and enables an unusual degree of replication plasticity under altered host conditions.

item.title: Cell: Extracellular matrix sensing regulates intratumoral heterogeneity of autophagic flux
item.description: Human pancreatic cancer cells sense specific components of the ECM to fine-tune their autophagy flux levels, conferring the ability to coordinate proliferation, survival, and responsiveness to chemotherapy. Targeting ECM sensing may turn this ability into a therapeutic opportunity.

item.title: Cell: A single-cell time-series atlas of endothelial cell embryonic development
item.description: The STED-EC atlas enables inter-organ and multi-time-point comparisons of gene expression in endothelial cells, revealing substantial transcriptomic variations across endothelial cells from different embryonic organs and facilitating investigation of previously unknown molecular mechanisms that govern organ-specific vascular development.

item.title: Cell: CLIM-TIME identifies metastatic microenvironment modulators for T cell therapy response
item.description: CLIM-TIME provides a high-throughput perturbation-mapping platform that links tumor suppressor gene loss to spatially defined metastatic niches and immune responses, identifying LOXL2 as a key modulator of suppressive metastatic environments. Inhibition of LOXL2 restores T cell infiltration into tumors and improves the efficacy of therapy.

item.title: Cell: Persistent T cell activation and cytotoxicity against glioblastoma following single oncolytic virus treatment in a clinical trial
item.description: Single oncolytic virus treatment in patients with glioblastoma induces deep and persistent T cell activation against tumor cells. Direct and sustained T cell engagement with tumor cells upon treatment correlates with survival outcome.

item.title: Cell: Planetary microbiome structure and generalist-driven gene flow across disparate habitats
item.description: A planetary-scale analysis of over 85,000 metagenomes establishes a framework for exploring the structure and drivers of global microbial habitats, revealing that generalist species bridge ecological boundaries to mediate gene flow across disparate habitats, including the dissemination of antimicrobial resistance.

item.title: Cell: Divergent tumor immunity determined by bacteria-cancer cell engagement
item.description: In a preclinical breast cancer metastasis model, the same bacteria strain, when present intracellularly versus extracellularly, exerts opposing effects on tumor immunity by inducing divergent neutrophil states, highlighting the intricacy in bacterial-host engagement for shaping tumor immunity.

item.title: Cell: Meningeal blood vessel blockage enhances anti-glioblastoma immunity
item.description: Meningeal blood vessel blockage enhances anti-tumor immunity against GBM in preclinical models by expanding dural resident border-associated macrophages, which are equipped with an elevated antigen-presentation function and are poised for effective T cell activation, suggesting a surgical strategy for potentiating GBM immunotherapy.

item.title: Cell: Molecular architecture of human dermal sleeping nociceptors
item.description: Integration of electrophysiology with single-cell transcriptomics defines the molecular signature of human dermal sleeping nociceptors and reveals oncostatin M as a selective modulator of these neurons in humans, providing a therapeutic entry point for neuropathic pain.

item.title: Cell: Hallmarks of cancer—Then and now, and beyond
item.description: Hanahan revisits the evolving framework of cancer hallmarks, synthesizing 25 years of conceptual refinement into a multidimensional view of tumor biology. This review highlights how aberrant capabilities, enabling traits, microenvironmental players, and systemic interactions converge to drive tumorigenesis and proposes that mechanism-guided co-targeting of hallmarks may offer promising therapeutic strategies.

item.title: Cell: Sympathetic-epithelial crosstalk governs tissue-resident memory T cell immunosurveillance in the skin
item.description: Sympathetic nerves regulate skin immunity by engaging keratinocytes to modulate the density of tissue-resident memory T cells. This neuro-epithelial axis can enable the nervous system to dynamically tune local immunosurveillance in barrier tissues against emerging cancers.

item.title: Cell: CRISPR screens in iPSC-derived neurons reveal principles of tau proteostasis
item.description: CRISPR screens in iPSC-derived neurons reveal that the E3 ubiquitin ligase CRL5 SOCS4 ubiquitinates tau, that CUL5 expression is correlated with resilience in human Alzheimer’s disease, and that electron transport chain dysfunction alters tau degradation by the proteasome.

item.title: Cell: An uORF-encoded mobile peptide sparks systemic stomatal immunity
item.description: In Arabidopsis , the uORF-encoded long-distance mobile peptide USIC in pathogen-infected local leaves activates systemic stomatal immunity, leading to stomatal closure in uninfected distal leaves.

item.title: Cell: A GPCR-G protein-β-arrestin megacomplex enabled by a versatile allosteric modulator
item.description: Identification of atazanavir as a pan-positive allosteric modulator for family A GPCRs that stabilizes a unique GPCR-G protein-β-arrestin megacomplex and mediates sustained signaling.

item.title: Cell: MYC binding to nascent RNA suppresses innate immune signaling by R-loop-derived RNA-DNA hybrids
item.description: RNA-binding-mediated multimerization of MYC concentrates RNA-degrading factors around double-stranded RNAs and R-loops. This prevents aberrant RNAs from accumulating and leaking into the cytosol. Through RNA binding, MYC suppresses innate immune signaling and promotes tumor growth.

item.title: Cell: Identification of Or5v1/Olfr110 as an oxylipin receptor and anti-obesity target
item.description: Or5v1/Olfr110, a high-affinity odor receptor, detects an oxylipin signal to boost liver fat burning and glucose control, and a synthetic agonist can amplify this metabolic benefit.

item.title: Cell: Mechanistic insights into fatty acid odor detection mediated by class II olfactory receptors
item.description: Cryo-EM structures reveal how Olfr110, a class II odorant receptor, binds hydrophobic odorants such as unsaturated fatty acid metabolites in a large polar pocket with an unconventional activation mechanism, defining the structural basis of odor recognition and guiding drug targeting.

item.title: Cell: Structural decoding of reversible covalent linkage of odorants in human olfactory receptor OR6A2
item.description: The human olfactory receptor OR6A2, re-engineered to be functional, demonstrates the mechanism by which it detects aldehydes. Using this approach, Wang, Wu, et al. uncovered a broadly conserved activation switch in class II odorant receptors. This work also outlines a practical approach to decode smell, with potential uses in fragrance design and inflammation therapy.

item.title: Cell: Nanoparticles hijack calvarial immune cells for CNS drug delivery and stroke therapy
item.description: Drug-loaded albumin NPs hijack calvarial immune cells to bypass the BBB via skull-meninges microchannels for CNS drug delivery and stroke therapy, establishing skull-based delivery and immune-assisted transport as a clinically translatable strategy for neurological therapeutics.

item.title: Cell: Human genetics guides the discovery of CARD9 inhibitors with anti-inflammatory activity
item.description: A binder-first approach enables the identification of a druggable pocket and compound for the immune protein CARD9 that dampens its inflammatory signaling. This compound reduces cytokine production in immune cells and in a mouse model, demonstrating how therapeutic modulation can mimic effects of a CARD9 variant protective against Crohn’s disease.
